producer_report.summary: I added a rendered-page convention and an xtask integration test that enforces it for the firstmate-work-handling page. The test builds the page with `xtask site --out <tmp>`, then checks three things. Word entries and the `#next-steps` link must come before the first transition card. The ids shown with the 'what this page cannot show' label must be exactly the model-limit findings in findings.json. Every transition card must say `(decided by X)` with X from the model's `trigger_evaluated_by`. A committed wrong page, `bad_firstmate_page.html`, is run through the same helpers by a test that requires each fault to be reported. All four tests in `xtask/tests/site_page.rs` pass, as does the policy scan. I did not run clippy or the full test suite. The convention is one sentence in the change producer prompt plus a fuller doc, `docs/conventions/rendered-page-assertions.md`. I also added a CHANGELOG entry, a mention in the existing D2-1 row of the requirements map (status unchanged), and a pointer comment in `site.rs`. One gap: the full Glossary section is rendered after the cards, so criterion 1 is only met for the early 'Words used first' entries (see open issues).

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test -p xtask` passes, including a new test that renders the real firstmate-work-handling study and asserts the glossary section and the `#next-steps` link both appear before the first transition card in the HTML.
criteria_check.evidence:
Ran `cargo test -p xtask --test site_page`: the order test passes. It builds the page with `xtask site --out ` and requires the 'Words used first' block and the `#next-steps` link before the first card, plus the next-steps and Glossary sections. Caveat: the full `

Glossary

` section is rendered after the cards, so only its existence is asserted; the early word entries are what come before the card. See open_issues. The full xtask suite was not run.

criteria_check.criterion: The new test asserts exactly which model-limit findings from studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json are present in the rendered HTML (and that others are absent), and `cargo test -p xtask` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_rendered_page_shows_exactly_the_model_limit_findings` passes. It derives the model-limit ids from findings.json (currently f3; the findings are in findings.json, not model.json) and requires the ids rendered with the 'what this page cannot show' label to match them exactly, so any other finding carrying that label fails.

criteria_check.criterion: The new test asserts that every transition whose model `trigger_evaluated_by` is `agent` is rendered as agent-decided, derived from model.json rather than hard-coded, and passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `the_rendered_page_shows_agent_decided_transitions_as_the_model_says` passes. For every transition in model.json it checks the card contains `(decided by <trigger_evaluated_by>)`, and it requires at least one agent-decided transition.

criteria_check.criterion: A committed fixture page (e.g. a deliberately wrong HTML file) is run through the same assertion helpers by a test that expects failure (glossary after first card, missing link, wrong findings, wrong evaluator), proving each check can fail; `cargo test -p xtask` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: xtask/tests/fixtures/bad_firstmate_page.html with `the_wrong_fixture_page_fails_every_check`, which runs the same three helpers and asserts each specific fault message. It passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The convention is written in a producer prompt/brief location (crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md, within its token headroom) stating: criteria about generated page contents require HTML assertions on `cargo run -p xtask -- site` output, run before handover, and failure blocks handover. Reader prompt and other budget-tight prompts are not grown.
criteria_check.evidence: One sentence added to producer.md saying that page-content criteria need HTML assertions on `cargo run -p xtask -- site` output, run before reporting, with failure blocking handover. The sentence is about 50 tokens by my estimate, under the 219 headroom stated in the reading. No other prompt was touched. I did not measure the budget with a tool.

criteria_check.criterion: The convention is also recorded in a doc under docs/ (stranger-readable) naming the xtask test as its enforcing mechanism.
criteria_check.evidence: docs/conventions/rendered-page-assertions.md names xtask/tests/site_page.rs and the fixture test as the enforcing mechanism.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` pass with no unrelated behavior changes to site rendering.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all`. The only change in site.rs is a comment, so rendering is unchanged.

open_issues:
Criterion 1 says the glossary section comes before the first transition card, but the real page renders `

Glossary

` after the cards, and changing the layout is out of scope. The test checks the 'Words used first' entries before the card and checks that the Glossary section exists. If the criterion means the Glossary section itself, the layout needs a separate decision.
I did not run the full `cargo test` suite or clippy.
mistakes: My first draft of the failure messages did not match what the fixture test expected, so the first run failed. I fixed the wording and it passed.
learnings: The xtask crate is a binary, so integration tests cannot import site.rs. The new test runs `CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask site --out <tempdir>`. `--out` must be outside the work tree or under the target directory.
findings.json holds f1 (could-not-run), f3 (model-limit) and f4 (could-not-run). There is no f2.
The full Glossary section is rendered after the transitions. The early 'Words used first' block, in Start here, is what precedes the first card.
Neither the producer prompt nor the new doc is mentioned in the policy test's lists, and the policy scan passes.
